clue.text: Three rivers, one discharging copiously

parts.note: the Po is the great river of northern Italy
the Ure is a Yorkshire river, a crossword regular
R is the standard abbreviation for river on maps

explanation.surface: A geography note about three rivers, one of them in heavy flood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Three rivers' supplies all three pieces in turn: two river names and the map abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that pours, especially heavily, is a pourer: a person or vessel letting liquid flow out freely.

clue.text: Put on too much weight to organise a do with lover

indicators.note: to organise is to arrange, so these letters are set out in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone overeats while arranging a party with their partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organise' rearranges the letters of A DO and LOVER; 'with' only joins the two fodder pieces, and 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To overload something is to burden it beyond its capacity, putting excessive weight or demand on it.

clue.text: Tail-end computer devices for night fliers

parts.note: the rear is the tail end of anything
mice are the pointing devices used with computers

explanation.surface: A hardware catalogue entry about mice for the back of a computer, then a twist into nature.
explanation.walkthrough: Reremouse or rearmouse is an old and dialect word for a bat, so its plural names bats; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Bats fly by night, and this archaic plural is a dialect name for bats.

clue.text: Putting in for payment for plaster

definitions.meaning: ... an account or bill means submitting it to be paid
a render is a coat of plaster or cement applied to a wall

explanation.surface: A builder submits a bill for the plastering work.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: presenting a bill for settlement, and the plaster coating spread on outside walls.

clue.text: Harry Lime's position in the field

definitions.meaning: Harry Lime is the title character of the 1949 film noir set in post-war Vienna, read here as Harry Lime is
a fielding position in cricket, behind the slips near the boundary

explanation.surface: Asks where a famous film villain plays when fielding in a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry Lime, Orson Welles's character, is the mysterious figure of the film's title; in cricket, the same three words name a fielder placed square behind the batsman on the off side.
explanation.definitionFit: The film's title character and a cricket fielding position share this same three-word name.

clue.text: Address to audience by proselytiser a produces transfer of power

indicators.note: said to an audience, the word is heard rather than read, so it is a sound-alike

parts.note: a talk is an address given to listeners
a proselytiser converts others to a faith, so is a converter

explanation.surface: A missionary's speech produces a shift in authority.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech TALK and TORQUE sound alike. 'by', the stray 'a' and 'produces' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A torque converter is a fluid coupling in automatic gearboxes that transmits engine power to the drive.

clue.text: Angler with one alternative: to take a new line

indicators.note: an alternative form of the letters is a rearranged one

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A fisherman with another option decides to change approach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alternative' rearranges ANGLER plus I; 'with' joins them and 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To realign is to set something on a fresh alignment or course, adopting a new line.

clue.text: Chamber for the maths set

definitions.meaning: an engine's ... is a chamber or pipe with several outlets
in mathematics a ... is a set of points forming a space that is locally flat

explanation.surface: Asks where the mathematics class is held.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a branched engine pipe or chamber and a topological space in mathematics.

clue.text: It shows who should be wearing the trousers, for example

definitions.text: It shows who should be wearing the trousers, for example

parts.words: It shows who should be wearing the trousers, for example
parts.note: sounds like the question of who is boss at home, but literally describes the sewn-in label naming a garment's owner

explanation.surface: A remark on which partner rules the household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing the trousers' is the idiom for being in charge; here it is literal, as in a school uniform label.
explanation.definitionFit: A sewn-in label printed with its owner's name, used on school clothes such as trousers.

clue.text: The keeper is an old servant

definitions.meaning: anything that retains or holds something in place is a keeper
a family ... is a long-serving servant

explanation.surface: The gamekeeper turns out to be a faithful old family servant.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a device that holds something, and a servant attached to a household for years.

clue.text: Showman almost stupefied after ban

indicators.note: after places the cut-down word behind the synonym for ban

parts.note: to bar is to ban

indicators.note: almost means one letter short, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: numb means dazed or stupefied

explanation.surface: An entertainer is left dazed after being barred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last letter of NUMB to leave NUM.
explanation.definitionFit: P. T. Barnum was the celebrated American circus impresario and showman.

clue.text: One may be burning to cheat admirer

parts.note: flam is an old word for a deception or cheat
a beau is a suitor or admirer

explanation.surface: Someone is keen to deceive the person courting them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A flambeau is a flaming torch, so it is something that may be alight.

clue.text: Motorway's access is not a suitable one

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main motorway, with the 1 read as the letter I, plus the possessive S
an access is a sudden attack or fit, as of rage

explanation.surface: A road sign says the slip road onto the motorway is unsuitable.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Yorkshire. 'access' is not a slip road but an outburst.
explanation.definitionFit: A misfit is someone or something that does not fit in, not suited to their setting.

clue.text: Farewell to the double feature

indicators.note: double means the piece is written twice in a row

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature

explanation.surface: A goodbye to a cinema showing two films.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the' are link words; 'double feature' looks like a cinema bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Chin-chin is an informal toast and also an old-fashioned way of saying goodbye.

clue.text: Sort of crime apparent during border Check tod pursuit

annotationWithheld.why: Held as 'Sort of crime apparent during border Check tod pursuit (6,3)': IN (during) + SIDE (border) + JOB (pursuit) fits, but 'apparent' and 'Check tod' are OCR garble with no job, and the scan is blank.
annotationWithheld.clue: Sort of crime apparent during border Check tod pursuit

clue.text: Move stealthily, dumping swag at the front, then run slowly

indicators.note: dumping means a letter is thrown out of the word

parts.note: to sidle is to move furtively

indicators.note: at the front picks the opening letter of swag

explanation.surface: A burglar creeps off, drops the loot near the door, then jogs away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dumping' removes S, the first letter of 'swag' ('at the front'), from SIDLE; 'then' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine that idles runs slowly while out of gear.

clue.text: Connive in liaison

definitions.meaning: to connive is to plot or scheme secretly
a liaison is a secret love affair

explanation.surface: Someone secretly takes part in an affair.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to scheme underhandedly and a clandestine love affair.

clue.text: Crustacean may be barnacled out east

indicators.note: may be suggests the letters of barnacled could form something else, once the letter for east is out

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A shellfish might be covered with barnacles in the far east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' rearranges BARNACLED with E (east) left 'out' of the result: BARNACLED holds the crab's letters plus E.
explanation.definitionFit: A land crab is a crab that lives mostly on land, a type of crustacean.

clue.text: Force a boundary

definitions.meaning: ... is incisive force or sharpness, as in a voice with an ...

explanation.surface: A batsman is urged to hit the ball over the rope.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means keenness or force, and the margin or border of something.

clue.text: Source of termites in garden consumed by anteater for one

indicators.note: in places the letter inside the combined pieces

parts.note: Eden is the biblical garden
ate means consumed

indicators.note: the source of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Termites from a garden are eaten by an anteater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like it puts termites inside the garden, but the letter sits inside the whole charade; 'consumed by' is not a container either, just the verb plus a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Edentates are toothless mammals, an order that includes anteaters, sloths and armadillos.

clue.text: Dope — ecstasy, speed — available in form

parts.note: gen is slang for information, as is dope
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
rate means speed

explanation.surface: A list of drugs sold in some form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' and 'speed' look like drugs, but mean information and pace; 'available in' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: To generate is to bring into being, which is a sense of to form.

clue.text: How bad the advertiser in the personal column used to feel?

definitions.text: How bad the advertiser in the personal column used to feel?

parts.words: How bad the advertiser in the personal column used to feel?
parts.note: the personal column was once called the agony column, so its advertisers are playfully said to be in torment

explanation.surface: Asks how miserable people placing lonely-hearts ads once felt.
explanation.walkthrough: The personal column of a newspaper was nicknamed the agony column.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in great distress or pain, like someone writing to the agony column.

clue.text: Rising Indian city getting in a state

indicators.note: getting in means the letter is placed inside
in a down clue rising means the word reads upwards, so backwards

parts.note: Ambala is a city in Haryana, northern India

explanation.surface: An Indian city grows and gets itself into a state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' turns AMBALA into ALABMA, and 'getting in' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabama is a state in the southern United States.

clue.text: Gunners face moving from the centre

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners
a dial is a clock face, and slang for a face

explanation.surface: Artillerymen face away from the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Radial means spreading out from a central point, like spokes.

clue.text: Expose new grandee as crook

indicators.note: crook is Australian slang for broken or out of order, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Reveals a new aristocrat to be a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crook' rearranges N plus GRANDEE; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To expose someone to danger is to endanger them, putting them at risk.

clue.text: Language applicable when English not available

indicators.note: not available means the letter is missing from the word

parts.note: germane means relevant or applicable

explanation.surface: A language becomes relevant when no English is spoken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: German is the language of Germany and Austria.

clue.text: Jat reverts to halma-playing in the mausoleum

indicators.note: reverts means it turns back, so the word reads backwards
playing suggests moving the pieces about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Jat goes back to playing halma, a board game, inside a famous tomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reverts' turns JAT into TAJ; 'playing' rearranges HALMA into MAHAL. A Jat is a member of a north Indian people; 'to' and 'in' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The Taj Mahal at Agra is the marble mausoleum built by Shah Jahan.

clue.text: One trying to influence jury to accept ruffians' leader

parts.note: to embrace an idea is to accept it

indicators.note: a word's leader is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone nobbling a jury takes on the gang's ringleader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' takes R from 'ruffians''; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Embracery is the old crime of trying to corrupt a jury, and the one committing it was so called.

clue.text: Officer cannot hope for rise to such a rank

definitions.text: Officer cannot hope for rise to such a rank

parts.words: Officer cannot hope for rise to such a rank
parts.note: describes an honorary promotion given to an officer that brings no rise in pay

explanation.surface: An officer despairs of being promoted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise' reads as promotion, but means a pay rise: this kind of rank gave the title without the higher pay.
explanation.definitionFit: A brevet is a commission giving an officer a higher nominal rank without corresponding pay.
